meta.titre: Commercial Banking Services: accounts, loans and everyday services
meta.sous_theme: Bank accounts, loans, overdrafts and banking documents

sections.contenu_markdown: A tailor in Yaounde is paid in cash by many customers. Keeping all that money at home is risky, so she opens an account at a commercial bank. Later she needs money to buy cloth in bulk, and the bank offers her a loan or an overdraft. Banks are used by traders every day, which is why the GCE Commerce papers ask which account earns interest, which document proves a deposit, and how a loan differs from an overdraft. This course covers all of these.

items: A bank is a business that accepts deposits and lends money.
Interest is the price paid for the use of money.
A percentage is a number out of one hundred.

sections.titre: What commercial banks offer and the documents they use
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Services of a commercial bank

- **Accepting deposits** and keeping money safe in accounts.
- **Lending money** as loans and overdrafts.
- **Payment services:** cheques, standing orders, bank drafts, transfers, cards and cash machines.
- **Safe custody** of valuable items and documents.
- **Foreign exchange:** changing one currency into another.
- **Advice** to customers on saving and borrowing.

### Types of account

| Account | Main features | Interest |
|---|---|---|
| Current | Money can be withdrawn at any time; cheque book; used for daily business payments | Usually none, or very little |
| Savings | For money kept for later; withdrawals are more limited; no cheque book in the usual case | Earns interest |
| Fixed (deposit) | Money is left for an agreed period; withdrawal before the end may be refused or penalised | Earns higher interest than ordinary savings |

### Main banking documents

- **Paying-in slip:** filled in when money is paid into an account; the bank stamps the copy as proof of the deposit.
- **Cheque:** a written order to the bank to pay money from the drawer's account.
- **Bank statement:** a list of all the money paid in and out of the account, sent to the customer, with the balance after each entry.

A main source of income for a bank is the difference between the interest it charges on loans and the interest it pays on deposits.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks for differences between two forms of borrowing
variantes.contenu_markdown:
| Point | Bank loan | Overdraft |
|---|---|---|
| Amount | A fixed sum paid to the customer at the start | The customer may spend up to an agreed limit above the balance |
| Interest | Charged on the whole sum for the whole period | Charged only on the amount overdrawn and only for the days it is overdrawn |
| Period | Usually medium or long term | Usually short term |
| Repayment | In agreed instalments | Repaid when money is paid into the current account |
| Account | Separate loan account | Used on a current account |

Write each difference as a pair: say what is true of the loan **and** what is true of the overdraft.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks for the interest earned on savings or paid on a loan
variantes.contenu_markdown: $$I = \frac{P \times R \times T}{100}$$ where $P$ is the sum, $R$ the rate per year (in %) and $T$ the time **in years**. For 400,000 FCFA at 3% for 2 years: $I = \frac{400\,000 \times 3 \times 2}{100} = 24\,000$ FCFA. For months, divide by 12: three months is $T = \frac{3}{12}$.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks what a bank does for a customer
variantes.contenu_markdown: A **standing order** pays a fixed amount at regular dates, a **bank draft** is a cheque issued by the bank itself, a **credit transfer** moves money directly between accounts, and a **debit card** lets the customer pay or withdraw cash from a machine.

sections.enonce_markdown: Mr Ako needs 150,000 FCFA for 3 months. Bank A offers a loan for 12 months at 10% per year simple interest. Bank B offers an overdraft at 14% per year, charged only on the amount overdrawn for the time it is overdrawn. Calculate the interest under each offer and advise Mr Ako.

etapes.justification: Both offers use simple interest, but the time must be in years. The overdraft lasts three months.
The loan is for the whole year and interest is charged on the full sum.
Three months is $\frac{3}{12}$ of a year.
Subtract the two amounts of interest.
The need lasts only three months. A loan charges interest for a full year on the whole sum, while an overdraft charges only for the time and amount used.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The overdraft is the better choice for a short, flexible need.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Loan interest is 15,000 FCFA and overdraft interest is 5,250 FCFA.** Mr Ako should take the overdraft, which is cheaper by 9,750 FCFA for a short need. If he needed the money for several years, a loan with fixed instalments would be more suitable.

items.erreur_markdown: 'A current account pays a high rate of interest.'
items.pourquoi_faux: A current account is designed for frequent payments. It usually pays no interest or very little. Savings and fixed accounts are the ones that earn interest.
items.correction_markdown: Current account: daily use, cheque book, little or no interest. Savings and fixed accounts: money kept for later, interest paid.

items.erreur_markdown: 'The bank statement is the slip that proves I paid money into my account.'
items.pourquoi_faux: The paying-in slip, stamped by the bank, is the proof of a deposit. A bank statement lists all entries, and it arrives later.
items.correction_markdown: Paying-in slip: shows a deposit made. Bank statement: shows all deposits, payments and the balance.

items.erreur_markdown: 'An overdraft is a fixed sum repaid in monthly instalments.'
items.pourquoi_faux: That describes a bank loan. An overdraft lets the customer draw more than the balance, up to a limit, and interest is charged only on the amount overdrawn.
items.correction_markdown: Loan: fixed sum, instalments. Overdraft: flexible, repaid by paying money into the current account.

items.erreur_markdown: 'Loan: pays interest.' 'Overdraft: pays interest.' (offered as a difference)
items.pourquoi_faux: Both carry interest, so this is not a difference. A difference compares a point on both sides.
items.correction_markdown: 'Interest on a loan is charged on the whole sum for the whole period, but on an overdraft only on the amount overdrawn.'

items.erreur_markdown: Using 3 for the time when the money is kept for 3 months
items.pourquoi_faux: The rate is per year, so time must be in years. Three months is not 3 years.

items.enonce_markdown: Which type of account would you advise for each person? (a) A trader who pays suppliers by cheque every week. (b) A parent who will not touch some money for a full year and wants it to earn the highest interest. Name also the document the trader should keep as proof of a deposit made at the counter.
items.solution_markdown: (a) A **current account**, because it comes with a cheque book and allows withdrawals at any time. (b) A **fixed (deposit) account**, because the money is left for an agreed period and earns higher interest. The document is the **stamped paying-in slip**.

items.enonce_markdown: A farmer places 500,000 FCFA in a savings account at 4% simple interest per year. Calculate the interest earned in 18 months and the total in the account at the end.

A shopkeeper's current account has an opening balance of 120,000 FCFA. During the month these entries occur in order: a deposit of 80,000 FCFA; a cheque of 45,000 FCFA paid by the bank; a standing order of 20,000 FCFA; a deposit of 35,000 FCFA; a cheque of 190,000 FCFA paid by the bank. (a) Show the balance after each entry in a table. (b) What is the position at the end of the month and what must the shopkeeper do? (c) Name two other services a commercial bank can offer this shopkeeper.
items.solution_markdown:
(a)

| Entry | Money in | Money out | Balance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opening balance | | | 120,000 |
| Deposit | 80,000 | | 200,000 |
| Cheque paid | | 45,000 | 155,000 |
| Standing order | | 20,000 | 135,000 |
| Deposit | 35,000 | | 170,000 |
| Cheque paid | | 190,000 | -20,000 |

(b) **The account is overdrawn by 20,000 FCFA.** The shopkeeper must pay money in to restore a positive balance, and should check whether the bank agreed an overdraft limit, because interest and charges may apply. (c) Any two: safe custody, foreign exchange, bank draft, credit transfer, cash machine card, advice on saving or borrowing.

items_markdown: A commercial bank accepts deposits, lends money, provides payment services, safe custody, foreign exchange and advice.
Current account: cheques, daily use, little or no interest. Savings and fixed accounts: money kept for later and earning interest, higher on fixed accounts.
A loan is a fixed sum charged interest on the whole amount for the whole period; an overdraft is flexible and charged only on the amount overdrawn and the time it is overdrawn.
The paying-in slip proves a deposit; the bank statement lists all entries and the balance.
Simple interest: $I = \frac{P \times R \times T}{100}$ with time in years.
When asked for differences, state both sides of each point.
